original_sentence: I have went to the store yesterday.
corrected_sentence: I went to the store yesterday.
mistakes: Wrong tense: with a past-time marker ("yesterday") use simple past "went", not present perfect "have gone". Also "have went" is never correct — past participle of "go" is "gone".

original_sentence: She is more taller than me.
mistakes: Double comparative: "more" + "-er" is redundant. Use either "taller" or "more tall" (and "taller" is the natural form).
"Agree" is a verb, not an adjective — don't pair it with "am". Just conjugate it directly: "I agree."

original_sentence: Can you explain me this problem?
corrected_sentence: Can you explain this problem to me?
mistakes: "Explain" takes the pattern "explain something to someone" — you can't put the indirect object directly after the verb the way you can with "tell" or "give".
1) "light weighted" → "lightweight": this compound adjective is always written as one word; 2) sentence-initial "they" should be capitalized.

original_sentence: in prod, we should use control DAG to stop it gracefully.
corrected_sentence: In prod, we should use the control DAG to stop it gracefully.
mistakes: 1) Capitalize "in" at the start of a sentence; 2) "control DAG" → "the control DAG": when referring to a specific known entity, use the definite article "the".

original_sentence: I've scheduled a meeting at April 27, 3 PM (Mon).
corrected_sentence: I've scheduled a meeting on April 27 at 3 PM (Mon).
mistakes: "at" → "on" for dates: use "on" with calendar dates (on April 27) and "at" with clock times (at 3 PM). The two prepositions serve different roles and shouldn't be swapped.

original_sentence: Just cant tell which one plays more import roles.
corrected_sentence: Just can't tell which one plays a more important role.
mistakes: 1) "cant" → "can't": missing apostrophe in the contraction; 2) "import" → "important": wrong word form — the adjective is needed here, not the noun/verb; 3) "more import roles" → "a more important role": "which one" refers to a single thing, so use the singular "role" with the article "a".

original_sentence: It does require a few hours tot make the permission take effect.
corrected_sentence: It does require a few hours for the permission to take effect.
mistakes: 1) "tot" → "to": typo/spelling error; 2) "to make the permission take effect" → "for the permission to take effect": the "for [noun] to [verb]" structure is the more natural English construction here.

original_sentence: @Niranjan Balasubramani can you confirm there is log coming in within last 48 h?
corrected_sentence: @Niranjan Balasubramani can you confirm there are logs coming in within the last 48h?
mistakes: 1) "there is log" → "there are logs": log entries are countable and plural, so the verb and noun both need to be plural; 2) "within last 48 h" → "within the last 48h": the definite article "the" is required before "last" in this time-range phrase.

original_sentence: it depends on how sensitive when it is about space complexity.
corrected_sentence: It depends on how sensitive it is when it comes to space complexity.
mistakes: 1) Capitalize "it" at sentence start; 2) "how sensitive" is an adjective dangling without a subject — it needs "how sensitive it is" (adjective + subject + verb); 3) "when it is about" → "when it comes to": "when it comes to X" is the natural fixed phrase in English meaning "regarding X".

original_sentence: it depends on how sensitive when talking about space complexity.
corrected_sentence: It depends on how sensitive you are when talking about space complexity.
mistakes: 1) Capitalize "it" at sentence start; 2) "how sensitive" is incomplete — needs a subject and verb: "how sensitive you are"; 3) "when talking about" is technically a dangling participle; clearer as "when you are talking about" to make the subject explicit.
